question: Should exact requester consumption of a descendant result count as terminal descendant delivery even when the requester's later outward delivery fails?
rationale: The patch is mechanically coherent, but choosing `delivered` makes a product-level reliability tradeoff by suppressing descendant retry and failure finalization after internal consumption; tests cannot decide that semantic boundary.

options.title: Accept consumption as delivery
options.body: Approve exact, run-ID-scoped requester consumption as terminal delivery after the contributor supplies restart, outward-failure, and negative-control runtime proof.

options.title: Track a distinct consumed state
options.body: Preserve requester consumption separately from delivered status so outward delivery or durable inbox settlement remains responsible for terminating retry behavior.

options.title: Fold into durable inbox work
options.body: Pause this branch and solve requester consumption within the broader durable completion inbox or spool contract tracked by the related delivery-loss work.

recommendation.title: Accept consumption as delivery
recommendation.body: Approve exact, run-ID-scoped requester consumption as terminal delivery after the contributor supplies restart, outward-failure, and negative-control runtime proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available recent current-main routing signal across the cron fallback and persisted subagent delivery-state surfaces affected by this decision.
